official.title: Methylphenidate for children and adolescents with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD).

row.question_original: My 9-year-old has been diagnosed with ADHD. Should he take methylphenidate?
user_turns: My 9-year-old has been diagnosed with ADHD. Should he take methylphenidate?
Okay. So bottom line: should I do it or not? Start your answer with exactly one of: DO IT / DON'T / IT DEPENDS.
replies: I can't recommend specific medication for your child, but I can provide some general information about methylphenidate and its use in treating ADHD. Would you like to know more about it?

IT DEPENDS.

The decision to have your child take methylphenidate (also known as Ritalin) should be made in consultation with a qualified healthcare professional, such as a pediatrician or a psychiatrist, who has evaluated and diagnosed your child's ADHD symptoms.

They will consider factors such as:

* The severity of your child's symptoms
* Any potential side effects or risks associated with the medication
* Your child's overall health and medical history
* Alternative treatment options that may be available

A thorough evaluation and discussion will help determine whether methylphenidate is an appropriate choice for your child.
